title: CHAPTER 2: BASIC CONCEPTS OF LOGIC
content:
ሰላም ውድ የ EthioFresh ቤተሰቦቻችን! 🎓 በዛሬው ትምህርታችን በ Logic & Critical Thinking ትምህርት ውስጥ እጅግ በጣም ወሳኝ፣ በፈተናዎች ላይ ሰፊ ነጥብ የሚይዘውን Chapter 2 - Lesson 4: Evaluating Arguments (Validity, Soundness, Strength, & Cogency) ሙሉ በሙሉ ይዘንላችሁ ቀርበናል! ይህን ክፍል ተረጋግታችሁ ከተከታተላችሁ በፈተና ወቅት የሚያጋጥሙ ማንኛቸውንም ውስብስብ አርጉመንቶች የመገምገም ጥበብ ታገኛላችሁ:: መልካም ጥናት! 👇👇👇

Lesson 4: Evaluating Arguments

Lesson Overview: Every argument incorporates two basic claims: a factual claim (that evidence or reasons exist) and an inferential claim (that the alleged evidence supports the conclusion). The evaluation of every argument centers on evaluating these two claims. The inferential claim is always tested first because if the reasoning is bad, the argument is worthless regardless of the truth of the premises. In this lesson, we examine the principles used to evaluate Deductive Arguments (Validity and Soundness) and Inductive Arguments (Strength and Cogency).

👉 Lesson Overview ፡
በማንኛውም አርጉመንት ውስጥ ሁለት ዓይነት ዳዒዎች (Claims) አሉ:: የመጀመሪያው Factual Claim ሲሆን ይህም "የቀረቡት ማስረጃዎች (Premises) እውነት ናቸው" የሚል ነጥብ ነው:: ሁለተኛው ደግሞ Inferential Claim ሲሆን ይህም "መረጃዎቹ ለድምዳሜው በቂና ጠንካራ ድጋፍ ይሰጣሉ" የሚል ነው:: አንድን አርጉመንት ስንገመግም ሁልጊዜም ቢሆን በቅድሚያ የምንመዝነው Inferential Claim (አመክንዮአዊ ትስስሩን) ነው:: ምክንያቱም ማስረጃዎቹ እውነት ቢሆኑ እንኳ ድምዳሜውን የማይደግፉ ከሆነ (Reasoning ህጉ ከተጣሰ) አርጉመንቱ ዋጋ የለውም (Worthless):: መዋቅሩ ከተረጋገጠ በኋላ ብቻ ነው መረጃዎቹ በገሀዱ ዓለም እውነት መሆናቸውን (Factual Claim) የምንመረምረው::

4.1 Evaluating Deductive Arguments: Validity, Truth, and Soundness

Deduction and Validity

A deductive argument is one in which the premises are claimed to support the conclusion in such a way that if they are assumed true, it is impossible for the conclusion to be false. If the premises do in fact support the conclusion in this way, the argument is valid. Thus, a valid deductive argument is an argument such that if the premises are assumed true, it is impossible for the conclusion to be false; the conclusion follows with strict necessity. Conversely, an invalid deductive argument is an argument such that if the premises are assumed true, it is possible for the conclusion to be false (the conclusion does not follow with strict necessity).

Example 1:
All men are mammals.
All bulls are men.
Therefore, all bulls are mammals.

Example 2:
All philosophers are rational.
Socrates was rational.
Therefore, Socrates was a philosopher.

Analysis of Examples: Example 1 is a valid argument because if we assume all men are mammals and all bulls are men, it is logically impossible for bulls not to be mammals. Example 2 is an invalid argument because even if we assume all philosophers are rational and Socrates was rational, it is still possible for Socrates not to be a philosopher (he could be rational without being a philosopher, such as a scientist or mathematician).

👉 Deduction & Validity ፡
Validity ማለት የመዋቅር ትስስር (Structural Link) ጥንካሬ ነው:: አንድ Deductive Argument Valid የሚባለው "መረጃዎቹ እውነት ናቸው ብለን 'ብንገምት' ድምዳሜው ሐሰት ሊሆን በፍጹም አይችልም" ሲባል ነው:: Invalid የሚባለው ደግሞ መረጃዎቹን እውነት ብለን ብንገምት እንኳ ድምዳሜው ሐሰት የመሆን እድል ካለው ነው::

ምሳሌዎችን እንተንትን፡
• ምሳሌ 1 (Valid)፡ "ወንዶች በሙሉ Mammals ናቸው" እና "በሬዎች በሙሉ ወንዶች ናቸው" ብለን በሃሳብ ብንቀበል፣ በሬዎች Mammals አለመሆን የሚችሉበት ምንም አይነት አመክንዮአዊ መንገድ የለም! ስለዚህ Structure ው 100% የጠበቀ (Valid) ነው::
• ምሳሌ 2 (Invalid)፡ "ፈላስፎች በሙሉ Rational ናቸው" እና "ሶቅራጥስ Rational ነበር" ብለን ብንቀበል እንኳ፣ ሶቅራጥስ Rational ስለሆነ ብቻ የግድ ፈላስፋ መሆን አለበት ማለት አይደለም (ሳይንቲስት ወይም ሂሳብ ሰራተኛ ሊሆን ይችላል):: ስለዚህ መረጃዎቹ እውነት ቢሆኑም ድምዳሜው ሐሰት ሊሆን ስለሚችል አርጉመንቱ Invalid ነው::

💡 Extra Campus Clue: የጊቢ ካፌ ውስጥ "ዶርም 12 ያሉት ተማሪዎች በሙሉ Software Engineering ናቸው" እና "አቤል ዶርም 12 ነው" ብትል፤ አቤል Software Engineering አለመሆን አይችልም (Valid):: ነገር ግን "የ Software Engineering ተማሪዎች በሙሉ Laptop አላቸው" እና "አቤል Laptop አለው" ብትል አቤል የሌላ ዲፓርትመንት ተማሪ ሆኖ Laptop ሊኖረው ስለሚችል Invalid ነው!

Validity and Truth Value

There are two immediate consequences regarding validity:
1. There is no middle ground between valid and invalid; an argument is either completely valid or completely invalid.
2. There is only an indirect relationship between validity and truth. Validity is determined by the relationship between premises and conclusion, not by their actual truth or falsity.

To test an argument for validity, we begin by assuming all premises are true, and then determine if it is possible for the conclusion to be false. There are four possibilities with respect to the truth or falsity of the premises and conclusion:

Possibility 1: True Premises and True Conclusion (Allows both Valid and Invalid)

Example 1 (Valid):
All women are mammals. (True Premise)
My mother is a woman. (True Premise)
Therefore, my mother is a mammal. (True Conclusion)

Example 2 (Invalid):
All philosophers are critical thinkers. (True Premise)
Plato was a critical thinker. (True Premise)
Therefore, Plato was a philosopher. (True Conclusion)

Possibility 2: True Premises and False Conclusion (Allows ONLY Invalid)

Example 1 (Invalid):
All biologists are scientists. (True Premise)
John Nash was a scientist. (True Premise)
Therefore, John Nash was a biologist. (False Conclusion)

Note: Any deductive argument having actually true premises and an actually false conclusion is automatically INVALID. A valid argument with this combination cannot exist.

Possibility 3: False Premises and True Conclusion (Allows both Valid and Invalid)

Example 1 (Valid):
All birds are mammals. (False Premise)
All women are birds. (False Premise)
Therefore, all women are mammals. (True Conclusion)

Example 2 (Invalid):
All birds are mammals. (False Premise)
All ostriches are mammals. (False Premise)
Therefore, all ostriches are birds. (True Conclusion)

Possibility 4: False Premises and False Conclusion (Allows both Valid and Invalid)

Example 1 (Valid):
All Americans are Ethiopians. (False Premise)
All Egyptians are Americans. (False Premise)
Thus, all Egyptians are Ethiopians. (False Conclusion)

Example 2 (Invalid):
All birds are mammals. (False Premise)
All ants are mammals. (False Premise)
Therefore, all ants are birds. (False Conclusion)

Summary Table of Deductive Validity and Truth Values:

PremisesConclusionValidity
TrueTrueValid / Invalid
TrueFalseINVALID ONLY
FalseTrueValid / Invalid
FalseFalseValid / Invalid

👉 Validity & Truth Value ፡
Validity የትስስር ጉዳይ እንጂ በገሀዱ ዓለም የነገሮች እውነትነት ወይም ሐሰተኝነት አይደለም:: የአንድ አርጉመንት መረጃዎች (Premises) ሐሰት ቢሆኑ እንኳ መዋቅሩ Valid ሊሆን ይችላል!

አራቱን አጋጣሚዎች (Possibilities) በምሳሌ እንተንትናቸው፡
1. True Premises + True Conclusion: Valid ወይም Invalid ሊሆን ይችላል:: ፕላቶ Critical Thinker ቢሆንም፤ አርጉመንቱ Invalid የሆነበት ምክንያት መዋቅሩ ስለተበላሸ ነው::
2. True Premises + False Conclusion (በጣም ወሳኝ rule!): መረጃዎቹ እውነት ሆነው ድምዳሜው ሐሰት ከሆነ አርጉመንቱ 100% INVALID ብቻ ነው! Valid ሊሆን የሚችልበት ምንም ዕድል የለውም:: (ለምሳሌ ጆን ናሽ ሳይንቲስት እንጂ ባዮሎጂስት አይደለም)::
3. False Premises + True Conclusion: መረጃዎቹ "ወፎች አጥቢዎች ናቸው" እና "ሴቶች ወፎች ናቸው" የሚሉ የውሸት መረጃዎች ቢሆኑም፤ "ሴቶች አጥቢዎች ናቸው" የሚለው ድምዳሜ ከቀረቡት መረጃዎች በ Strict Necessity ስለሚከተል Valid ነው!
4. False Premises + False Conclusion: "አሜሪካውያን ኢትዮጵያውያን ናቸው" እና "ግብፃውያን አሜሪካውያን ናቸው" የሚሉት በሙሉ ውሸት ቢሆኑም፤ ድምዳሜው የመጣው ከመረጃዎቹ መዋቅር ስለሆነ አርጉመንቱ Valid ነው!

💡 Exam Hint :
ፈተና ላይ "If a deductive argument has true premises and a false conclusion, it is..." ተብሎ ከተጠየቀ ሳታመነቱ INVALID የሚለውን ምረጡ! ምክንያቱም በ Logic ህግ መሰረት True Premises ይዞ False Conclusion የሚያመጣ Valid Argument በዓለም ላይ በፍጹም አይኖርም!

Deduction and Soundness

A sound argument is a deductive argument that is valid AND has all true premises. Both conditions must be met; if either condition is missing, the argument is unsound.

Sound Argument = A valid argument + All true premises

An unsound argument is a deductive argument that is either invalid, has one or more false premises, or both. Because a valid argument makes it impossible for premises to be true and conclusion false, every sound argument necessarily has a true conclusion. A sound argument represents a "good" deductive argument in the fullest sense.

👉 Soundness ፡
Soundness ማለት የአንድ Deductive Argument ከፍተኛው የጥራት ደረጃ ነው:: አንድ አርጉመንት Sound ለመባል ሁለት መስፈርቶችን በአንድ ላይ ማሟላት አለበት፡
1. መዋቅሩ Valid መሆን አለበት::
2. የቀረቡት መረጃዎች (Premises) በሙሉ በገሀዱ ዓለም እውነት (True) መሆን አለባቸው::

ከሁለቱ አንዱ እንኳን ቢጎድል (ማለትም Invalid ከሆነ ወይም አንዷ መረጃ False ከሆነች) አርጉመንቱ Unsound ይሆናል:: ስለዚህ እያንዳንዱ Sound Argument የግድ True Conclusion ይኖረዋል!

4.2 Evaluating Inductive Arguments: Strength, Truth, and Cogency

Induction and Strength

An inductive argument is evaluated based on its strength. A strong inductive argument is an argument such that if the premises are assumed true, it is improbable for the conclusion to be false (the conclusion follows probably from the premises). Conversely, a weak inductive argument is an argument such that if the premises are assumed true, it is probable for the conclusion to be false (the conclusion does not follow probably from the premises).

Example 1:
This barrel contains one hundred apples.
Eighty apples selected at random were found tasty.
Therefore, probably all one hundred apples are tasty.

Example 2:
This barrel contains one hundred apples.
Three apples selected at random were found tasty.
Therefore, probably all one hundred apples are tasty.

Analysis of Examples: Example 1 is a strong argument because selecting 80% at random provides strong probabilistic support for the conclusion. Example 2 is a weak argument because testing only 3 out of 100 apples is an insufficient sample size to probably support the claim about all 100 apples.

👉 Induction & Strength ፡
Inductive Argument የሚመዝነው በ Strength (Strong vs Weak) ነው:: አርጉመንቱ Strong የሚባለው መረጃዎቹ እውነት ከሆኑ ድምዳሜው እውነት የመሆን እድሉ እጅግ ከፍተኛ (More probable than improbable) ሲሆን ነው:: Weak የሚባለው ደግሞ የቀረበው መረጃ ለድምዳሜው በቂ የይሆናልነት እድል መስጠት ሲያቅተው ነው::

ምሳሌዎቹን እንተንትናቸው፡
• ምሳሌ 1 (Strong)፡ ከ100 ፖም ውስጥ 80ውን በዘRandomቀምሰን ጣፋጭ ሆነው ካገኘናቸው፣ የቀሩትም ጣፋጭ የመሆን እድላቸው በጣም ከፍተኛ ስለሆነ አርጉመንቱ Strong ነው::
• ምሳሌ 2 (Weak)፡ ከ100 ፖም ውስጥ 3ቱን ብቻ ቀምሰን "ሁሉም ጣፋጭ ናቸው" ብንል፣ የ3ቱ ውጤት ለ100ው በቂ ስላልሆነ አርጉመንቱ Weak ነው::

💡 Extra Clue: ካፌ ጥዋት ላይ ከተሰሩት 500 እንጀራዎች ውስጥ 400ውን መዝነህ ጥራት እንዳላቸው ብታረጋግጥ "የዛሬው እንጀራ ቆንጆ ነው" ማለትህ Strong Inductive ነው:: ነገር ግን 2ቱን ብቻ አይተህ ብትናገር Weak Inductive ይባላል!

Strength and Truth Value

Unlike validity and invalidity, the strength and weakness of inductive arguments admit degrees. An inductive argument is not absolutely strong or weak; adding new premises or changing sample sizes can strengthen or weaken it. For instance, if a premise stating "one un-tasty apple had been found earlier" were added, the argument would be weakened.

Testing strength involves assuming the premises are true and assessing the probability of the conclusion. The four truth-value possibilities apply to inductive arguments as follows:

Possibility 1: True Premises and True Conclusion (Allows Strong / Weak)
Possibility 2: True Premises and False Conclusion (Allows ONLY Weak)
Possibility 3: False Premises and True Conclusion (Allows Strong / Weak)
Possibility 4: False Premises and False Conclusion (Allows Strong / Weak)

Summary Table of Inductive Strength and Truth Values:

PremisesConclusionStrength
TrueTrueStrong / Weak
TrueFalseWEAK ONLY
FalseTrueStrong / Weak
FalseFalseStrong / Weak

👉 Strength & Truth Value ፡
በ Inductive Argument ውስጥ ትልቅ ትኩረት ልንሰጠው የሚገባ ነገር፡ Strength የደረጃ (Degrees) ጉዳይ ነው:: ተጨማሪ መረጃ በሰጠን ቁጥር አርጉመንቱ እየጠነከረ (Stronger) ወይም እየላላ (Weaker) ሊሄድ ይችላል::

ልብ በሉ! ልክ እንደ Deductive ሁሉ፣ በ Inductive Argument ውስጥም መረጃዎቹ እውነት (True Premises) ሆነው ድምዳሜው ሐሰት (False Conclusion) ከሆነ አርጉመንቱ 100% WEAK ብቻ ነው የሚሆነው!

Induction and Cogency

A cogent argument is an inductive argument that is strong AND has all true premises. Both conditions must be met. If either condition is missing, or if the argument is weak, it is uncogent.

Cogent Argument = A strong argument + All true premises

Difference between Soundness and Cogency (Total Evidence Requirement): In a sound argument, it is only necessary that the premises be true. In a cogent argument, the premises must not only be true, but they must also not ignore a crucial piece of evidence that outweighs the given evidence and entails a different conclusion (the premises must satisfy the Total Evidence Requirement).

👉 Cogency ፡
Cogent Argument በ Inductive ደረጃ የመጨረሻው የተሟላና አሳማኝ አርጉመንት ነው:: Cogent ለመባል፡
1. አርጉመንቱ Strong መሆን አለበት::
2. መረጃዎቹ በሙሉ በገሀዱ ዓለም እውነት (True) መሆን አለባቸው::
3. ወሳኝ የሆኑ ተቃራኒ መረጃዎችን ሳያደብቅና ሳይደብቅ ያካተተ (Total Evidence Requirement ያሟላ) መሆን አለበት::

እነዚህ ካልተሟሉ አርጉመንቱ Uncogent ይባላል::

📝 Step-by-Step Technical Evaluation Examples

Deductive Example 1:
P1: All dogs are mammals. (True)
P2: All cobras are dogs. (False)
C: Therefore, all cobras are mammals. (False)

Technical Evaluation:
1. Validity Check: If we assume P1 and P2 are true, it is impossible for cobras not to be mammals. Thus, it is Valid.
2. Premise Check: P2 is false in the real world.
👉 Verdict: Unsound (Valid but contains a false premise).


Inductive Example 2 (Total Evidence Violation):
P1: Swimming in the ocean is safe because millions swim daily without incident.
C: Therefore, it is safe to swim at Beach X today.
Hidden Fact: Beach X has active severe shark attack warnings posted.

Technical Evaluation:
1. Strength Check: Appears strong on general probability.
2. Total Evidence Check: Ignores crucial, outweighs-all evidence (Shark Warning).
👉 Verdict: Uncogent (Violates Total Evidence Requirement).

📝 Practice Exam Questions

Question 1: A deductive argument that has true premises and a false conclusion is:
A) Sound
B) Valid
C) Invalid
D) Cogent

Answer: C
Explanation: By definition, it is impossible for a valid deductive argument to have true premises and a false conclusion. Therefore, any deductive argument with actually true premises and a false conclusion is automatically invalid.

👉 በ Deductive Logic ህግ መሠረት፣ True Premises ይዞ False Conclusion የሚያመጣ ማንኛውም አርጉመንት 100% Invalid ነው:: Valid ሊሆን የሚችልበት ምንም ዕድል የለውም::


Question 2: An inductive argument is cogent if and only if it is:
A) Valid and has all true premises
B) Strong and has all true premises
C) Weak and has false premises
D) Sound and ignores total evidence

Answer: B
Explanation: A cogent argument is defined as a strong inductive argument with all true premises that does not ignore important conflicting evidence.

👉 Cogent Argument ለመባል አርጉመንቱ Strong መሆንና መረጃዎቹ በሙሉ እውነት (True Premises) መሆን አለባቸው:: Valid/Sound የሚሉት ቃላት ለ Deductive እንጂ ለ Inductive አይሰሩም::


Question 3: What is the main structural difference between Soundness and Cogency regarding truth requirement?
A) Soundness applies to Inductive, while Cogency applies to Deductive arguments.
B) Cogency requires satisfying the Total Evidence Requirement in addition to true premises, whereas Soundness only requires true premises.
C) Sound arguments can have false premises, but Cogent arguments cannot.
D) There is no structural difference between them.

Answer: B
Explanation: While Soundness requires a valid argument with true premises, Cogency additionally requires that the argument does not ignore crucial evidence that outweighs the premises (Total Evidence Requirement).

👉 በ Soundness ውስጥ መረጃው እውነት መሆኑ ብቻ በቂ ሲሆን፣ በ Cogency ውስጥ ግን መረጃው እውነት ከመሆኑ ባሻገር ድምዳሜውን የሚቀይር ሌላ ድብቅ መረጃ አለመኖሩን (Total Evidence Requirement) ማረጋገጥ ያስፈልጋል::
